P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No surrender or conversion requirement. The 1997 Law on Foreign Exchange provides that there is no restriction on foreign-exchange operations through authorised banks (Art. 5). Banks must report each transfer of USD 10,000 or more to the National Bank of Cambodia (Art. 17). Travellers carrying USD 10,000 or more in cash must declare it to customs. The economy is heavily dollarised.

sources.title: Foreign Exchange (CDC investment guide)
sources.quote: Restriction on the Foreign Exchange The “Law on the Foreign Exchange” of September 1997 stipulates that “there shall be no restriction on foreign exchange operations” through authorized banks (Article 5) but the authorized banks shall report to the National Bank of Cambodia the amount of each transfer equaling or exceeding 10,000 US dollars (Article 17).

P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Residents are allowed to hold foreign currencies freely (Law on Foreign Exchange, Art. 7), and USD accounts are commonplace.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole proprietorship registers online with the Ministry of Commerce through its Business Registration portal or the CamDX 'Single Portal'. Sign-in uses CamDigiKey, there is no minimum capital and liability is unlimited. Per Deel, foreign nationals aged 18+ with valid ID can also register. Registration with the General Department of Taxation is required within 15 working days of starting business or MoC registration (per a 2015 law-firm note). Current fees were not captured.

L2_tax_id.answer: A sole proprietor registers with the General Department of Taxation (GDT) through the e-Tax Services portal (e-registration) to get a taxpayer account and number, and registers for 10% VAT if applicable. This follows business registration with the Ministry of Commerce (Deel).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident taxpayers are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents only on Cambodian-source income. Consulting and self-employment income is outside salary tax and falls under the tax on income (profit tax). Physical persons and sole proprietorships pay annual progressive rates of 0% up to KHR 18m, rising to 20% above KHR 150m. The same rates apply to small taxpayers, a classification that starts at KHR 250m annual turnover for sole proprietors in service sectors. Under the 2023 Law on Taxation regime there is a minimum tax of 1% of turnover.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 10% for self-declaration-regime taxpayers. Exported goods and services rendered outside Cambodia are zero-rated. Per Emerhub, registration is triggered by turnover above KHR 60 million (about USD 14,600) in three consecutive months for services, or KHR 125 million for goods.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: No comprehensive data-protection law is in force. A draft Law on Personal Data Protection was released on 23 July 2025 and was still not enacted as of mid-February 2026. It is expected to apply after a two-year implementation period from promulgation. Sectoral rules, including the 2019 E-commerce Law's consumer-data provisions, apply meanwhile.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: The E-commerce Law and the Consumer Protection Law were both enacted on 2 November 2019. The E-commerce Law covers domestic and cross-border e-commerce, with consumer-protection provisions on information, scams and data protection, and may subject service providers and intermediaries to licensing. The Consumer Protection Law applies to anyone trading with consumers in Cambodia. A statutory cancellation or cooling-off right for online purchases was not found.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
